pilot-01: Opening must show user looking at a map before NPC comments. Keep current 7-node plot but remove unrealistic accessibility recommendations: measured-looking slope is not proof a path is accessible. aa records a candidate approach pending width/slope checks and park confirmation.

Never squeeze through hedges, scratch sleeves, crawl under gates or trespass. b and ba follow an obvious public paved path OUTSIDE the locked boundary; the choice is whether to take time to trace it or document the dead end.
bb must mark NPC personal paper map/notebook, never write on the public map board. Make all Chinese lines faithfully match revised English.
pilot-02: The real park-notes scene is a park rest area with the bridge in the DISTANCE and runners nearby. User is writing observations in a notebook. Never start or teleport under a bridge or walk to its pillars. Revise the whole story around listening from this park spot: rhythmic sounds from runners, intermittent bridge traffic and a nearby loose bench fitting. Do not repeat the lost/blown-paper plot.
Make the two second-stage choices test different hypotheses, not arbitrary left/right starts. End with tentative observations, not confident false acoustic proofs or invented user talent.

No recording user at all, including humming. Characters can listen, mark patterns, or use NPC own recorder for a self-produced sound. No consent choice that silently authorizes using user audio in a theatre show. All endings concretely resolve one observation.
pilot-03: Opening must show USER writing a short postcard at the pond before Ruth offers her own related puzzle. Never accuse user of reading over her shoulder.

Remove ALL numerical word counts and word-limit numbers. Current claimed counts are wrong (Harrow Meadow Saturday noon is four words, not six; fourteen is not too long for seventeen). Theme can be limited space and deliberate blank space without arithmetic. Change title accordingly.

Every invitation version must retain venue, day AND time, otherwise unusable. All versions can include fictional Harrow Meadow / Saturday / noon consistently. Clarify brevity is her personal constraint, not physical impossibility.

Court stenographers record speech; never imply her job was catching liars. The drafting history and crossed-out words must be visible to user before being referenced. For a.ab avoid claiming a reason user never actually supplied; let Ruth provide field flooding as known fact herself.
pilot-04: Rewrite around FOUR numbered paper draw tokens whose written numbers are 1,2,3,4 and a saved photo. No private participant names. On start USER offers nearby napkins; Morgan accepts before help. Napkins only blot water. Replacement tokens must all be the same size/material so physical differences cannot bias a draw.

Keep two branches: make a fresh complete identical-paper set from verified photo, or keep originals for a display/memento and use verified numbers in a separate equal-token set. Never put ambiguous Ma? or uncertain entries into a draw. Majority votes cannot determine a true name/number.

No teleport from cafe to hall or unexplained signup sheet on wall. NPC has supplies/photo or can ask cafe staff for scrap paper. All endings finish a fair complete set or explicitly defer the draw pending confirmation. Choices should change practical method and interpersonal detail, not compromise fairness.
Preserve competitive-but-learning character. Do not turn them instantly into someone who romanticizes all damage or claims every stain is valuable.
pilot-06: Opening must have user already at cafe window watching rain; NPC starts from shared observation, not inventing user wet coat or moving them into the seat. Remove claim electrical apprentice checked this cafe roof this morning.

Paper strips cannot absorb ambient street smell instantly: explicitly use a labelled pre-scented test strip from her tin, and ask before offering it. Never assert user has smelled it or likes it unless chosen.

All four endings must be COMPLETE prewritten scenes. Remove "whatever you suggest", "you offer yours", "your turn", and any ending waiting for a nonexistent free-text input. Where user names something, place the EXACT name/words in preceding choice. Use NPC to propose and complete a word puzzle otherwise.
Keep three sounds concrete (road, window, drain) but avoid forcing a pointless rhyme or requiring an additional unimplemented user turn. Chinese must contain no unlocalized English titles.
pilot-05: pond-sketch action starts with USER holding their own sketchbook and choosing tree vs reflection. Daniel can have his OWN sketchbook too and compare it, but explicitly establish both books; do not transfer user book to NPC or assume user is an expert. Keep choices about Daniels book once he asks.

Explain physical causes correctly: wind alone cannot drag a pencil held by a person. The accidental stroke comes from Daniel shifting his own elbow. Never assert a football call right/wrong without context. Reduce repetitive numbered lists so personality is visible but not caricature.

All four endings must leave the page in genuinely different states (integrated streak, clean reflection, annotated accidental line, deliberately cropped tree). Do not repeat identical biography in every terminal.
pilot-08: The real scene is a park rest area looking at a bridge in the DISTANCE, not a bench by a pond. User has coffee. Nora must not identify distant peoples jobs, fear, hidden intention, ages, or motives from gait. She can observe pace and explicitly admit she cannot know why.

Remove unsolicited judgments of user fear, "Good, that means you know what it costs", "never scared people are useless", and disguised life coaching. Her character values boundaries and gentle observation, not judging strangers as a lesson.

Summary must match card and story: never say learned swimming at 58 while dialogue says 50. Use no age-of-learning number in summary. No recording strangers without permission; oral-history hobby is opt-in interviews.

Current b choice offering to hold a cup while she holds it is incoherent and Chinese reveals a result before choice. Replace with a clear offer to move cold cup to stable ledge, versus leave it alone and ask about her work. Terminal ba must honor chosen offer without scolding user. No cup placed on known wobbly arm.
pilot-09: Use BINOCULARS, not telescope: the authored scene has binoculars on the stone platform. Ask whose they are / establish NPC owns them before user takes them.
Do not assert "nature does not do straight" or diagnose a quick-release knot as definite geocache evidence. Use observable clues and qualified hypotheses. No invented scientific certainty.

All terminals need a finished small action, no "should we leave a reply" or "would you look for notice with me" awaiting unimplemented input. NPC may make their own note and finish. Remove time-of-day assertions about someone sailing this morning.

Keep same underlying setup across paths: local model-boat group has a temporary tow line, identified partly or fully depending on choice. Do not turn it into a mysterious sentimental message conveniently left for user.
pilot-10: Current park-map setting provides park paths and distant bridge, not a theatre/observatory. No teleport into new buildings, no invented visitor opening hours. Old path follows waterside, new path stays in park and reaches a bench. At bench NPC can take out OWN folded costume repair/photo and OWN printed star wheel from bag; no requirement to see stars or know time of day.

a branches can preserve the swan vs delivery-cart story with honest labelling. b choices should be examining his printed star wheel versus helping phrase a short proposed repair offer; ba completes rotating/reading printed diagram without actual sky claims, bb completes a concrete draft note he chooses to keep for later. No messages sent on users behalf.
Opening explicitly begins from USER looking at map with Victor nearby. Narration should use You consistently, not unexplained third-person They. Fix duplicated words in Chinese summary.
